kind: independent fixture definitions only, not implementation or executed evidence
status: prepared for review; Q1 not run

oracle_provenance.basis: Approved 0-to-1 transition, publication/repaint rules and literal independent expected outcomes. Pixel inputs use transcribed glyph masks from the immutable accepted raw character asset, not generated descriptor IDs or the observer/parser.
oracle_provenance.mask_orientation: Raw arcade glyphs rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise; each mask byte is one left-to-right display scanline.

wire_definition.note: This is fixture data, not a new live transport protocol. Fake tools supply literal memory bytes/code/dump files to the actual new acquisition path. Expected classifications below are authored constants, never generated by that path.
wire_definition.integer_order: 6809 16-bit values are big-endian; commit subtraction is modulo 65536.
wire_definition.memory_hex: Address keys are logical CPU read starts; each value is a literal contiguous byte sequence. 0x00df covers MENU_PREV, MENU_SELECT, MENU_DIRTY. 0x008f covers FRONT, BACK, pending, commit high and low.
wire_definition.pixel_reference: Selects the literal two-label scanline bank below. Null means no pixel read is admitted at that stop.
wire_definition.seed: First post-publication stop establishes the counter only; the next delta-one stop supplies the visible baseline.
wire_definition.input_marker: menu_down is before the selection increment, so selection 0 there is expected.
wire_definition.release: MENU_PREV down bit 2 must become clear after the event before final stability interpretation. A later visual report may remain pending without extending automated observation.
wire_definition.classification_priority: Retain independent cleanup/timeout facts. Reject identity/mapping or malformed acquisition before product interpretation; exclude repeated/held input and screen transition before diagnosing selection or pixels. Invalid input retains result_class=incomplete with menu_outcome=invalid_fixture; a screen transition is an observed separate outcome, not a successful menu fixture. A confirmed product failure does not require collecting the rest of the passing-case stability samples.

capture_cases.risk: Complete independent base trace; marker precedes increment; both owner repaints and follow-ups; raw PAR upper bits do not determine page identity.
Counter wraps once without losing publication coverage.
Missed successful publication cannot be counted as consecutive coverage.
A queued pre-input image and a still-dirty owner are not stale-display failures; their pixels must not be read.
Wrong readable PAR page must stop pixel acquisition before interpretation.
Wrong live publication-code bytes invalidate the source-derived display inference.
Two observed Down events invalidate the one-press fixture instead of proving state corruption.
No recorded release makes the one-press fixture invalid; user timing alone is insufficient.
Selection reverses after confirmed release with one event and no screen change.

expected.note: The observed product failure is sufficient; the observer may stop without collecting later stability samples.

capture_cases.risk: An ordinary screen/mode transition must not be misreported as state corruption.
Selection remains 1 and both repaint bits cleared, but B follow-up restores the old highlight.

expected.note: The observed product failure is sufficient; the observer may stop without collecting later stability samples.

capture_cases.risk: No Down event before the native deadline is missing coverage, not a successful test.
Missing A follow-up is incomplete even when all earlier samples look correct.
Truncated returned framebuffer-state bytes cannot be interpreted as product state.
User-reported flicker is retained when complete machine samples do not capture its cause.
A no-publication IRQ is ignored rather than counted toward four required post-input publications.
A missing later user visual report is pending manual evidence, not an automated timeout or a claim of no flicker.

host_time_units: milliseconds relative to one simulated Windows monotonic T0; limits 10000 startup, 40000 native work, 55000 native finalization, 60000 host total

host_cases.risk: Successful two-operation host handoff budgets startup/work/cleanup/receipt together.
Late READY must never start delayed work.
Host control loss after GO must cancel all owned native work.
Command failure is retained with its own result and is not retried.
Unconfirmed owned cleanup at host deadline must not pass or extend the operation.
A zero process exit without a native receipt is incomplete.
Missing readiness prevents live dispatch; Q1 itself requires no human key press.
An occupied evidence root is preserved rather than cleared or overwritten.
Native work timeout includes child cleanup and a receipt before the outer host limit.

required_acquisition_obligations: Replay fixtures through the actual new GDB-script/result acquisition and classifier, with controlled fake tools.
Validate code and readable mapping before requesting any label pixel bytes.
Do not request pixel spans at the seed, input marker, zero-delta IRQ or still-dirty owner.
Read each eight-scanline label span at base + row*160 with its own 40/28-byte row width.
Do not read write-only task/video control addresses as configuration.
No real emulator, debugger, key injection, game build, or retry is part of offline Q1.
Use the actual host-dispatch code with a fake process adapter and simulated clock; do not test a second implementation of its policy.
Run the selected TOOL019 class only; preserve the baseline suite and evidence.
